facts.text: Alamance was the site of the largest conflict of the War of the Regulation on May 16, 1771, where Governor William Tryon defeated 2,000 Regulators.
In 1849, the Holt family converted a spinning mill into a loom mill that produced the first factory‑dyed cotton cloth south of the Potomac, known as Alamance Plaids.
The Holt family expanded beyond textiles, building dozens of mills across North Carolina while also shaping banking, railroads, and state politics.
Stroll through Alamance’s historic downtown, where local boutiques and farm‑to‑table restaurants line Main Street.
Spend a day on a historic farm and experience life as it was in 1830, right here in Alamance.
Alamance once earned the nickname ‘Courduroy Capital of the World’ and still hosts a fabulous 1920s Art Deco theatre.
